msg: Ultra on root: The tm_dot_prod loop dominates (95.7% of cycles). Each iteration processes 8 int8 pairs: 16 byte loads (5 cycles each), 8 multiplies (5-6 cycles), 7 adds (3 cycles), and loop overhead. The 4-byte alignment allows loading 4 elements per 32-bit word. A custom instruction that consumes two 32-bit registers (each holding 4 int8 values) and returns a 32-bit result can replace 8 loads, 4 multiplies, and 3 adds with 2 loads and 1 custom instruction, yielding ~6-8× speedup on the hotspot.

proposal.title: 4-element int8 dot product (full reduction)
proposal.rationale: Computes the exact sum of 4 products in one combinational step (4×8×8 multipliers + adder tree). Replaces 4 lb + 4 mul + 3 add (≈41 cycles) with 1 lw + 1 dot4 (≈11 cycles). Two dot4 per 8-element chunk plus one add yields ~25 cycles/8 elements vs. 156 baseline → ~6.2× hotspot speedup. Fits area: 4 DSP multipliers + ~150 LUTs for adders (~3.5% LUT increase).

proposal.title: Two independent 2-element dot products (packed 16+16)
proposal.rationale: Produces two 16-bit partial sums (each fits: 2×127×127=32258 < 32767). Uses 4 multipliers + 2 adders (no final adder). Saves one adder level vs. dot4 (~10% less LUTs). Software must unpack and add four 16-bit values per 8 elements → extra 2-3 instructions. Estimated 25+ cycles/8 elements → ~5.5× hotspot speedup. Area ~3.2%.

proposal.title: 4-element dot product with pairwise 16-bit sums
proposal.rationale: Same hardware as dot2x2 but pairs (0,1) and (2,3) instead of (0,1) and (2,3) — actually identical pairing; distinct only in naming. Provides same two 16-bit sums. Software usage identical to dot2x2. Included to show pairing variation; speedup/area same as dot2x2.

proposal.title: 4-element dot product with cross-pair 16-bit sums
proposal.rationale: Cross-pairing (0,2) and (1,3) enables alternative register scheduling: software can interleave loads to reduce pressure. Same 4 multipliers + 2 adders. Cycle count identical to dot2x2. Area ~3.2%.

proposal.title: 2-element dot product on low halves of registers
proposal.rationale: Uses only 2 multipliers + 1 adder (low 16 bits of each register). Smaller area (~1.8% LUTs). Software must shift registers to process all 4 elements: 4 calls per 8 elements (two words, each needs lo and hi). More instructions but still eliminates 12 multiplies and 12 loads. Estimated 35 cycles/8 elements → ~4.5× hotspot speedup.

proposal.title: 2-element dot product on high halves of registers
proposal.rationale: Complement to dot2_lo; same area/speedup. Allows processing high half without shift if compiler keeps values in upper half. Distinct opcode but same hardware cost. Combined with dot2_lo gives full 4-element coverage with two instructions per word.

msg: Ultra on n5: The measured region is dominated by tm_dot_prod (73% cycles), which processes 8 int8 elements per loop iteration using four ss_dot2_lo calls (two per 32-bit word for low/high halves) plus 4 shifts, 5 adds, 4 loads, and a branch. The ss_dot2_lo intrinsic itself accounts for 19.5% of dynamic instructions. The bottleneck is the scalar reduction of four 16-bit partial products per 8-element chunk, requiring explicit shifts and adds that a wider reduction or high-half instruction could eliminate. The requant hotspot (1.7%) uses a 32x16 multiply-shift sequence amenable to a fused multiply-high instruction.

Ultra on n1: The main loop (tm_dot_prod, 40% of instructions) executes 4096 iterations of 8-element dot products using two ss_dot4 calls (47.9% of instructions) plus loop overhead (loads, adds, branch). The requant function (2.75%) performs per-channel fixed-point scaling and clamping. The tail loop is never executed (size=512 is multiple of 8). Custom instructions can only replace arithmetic with two 32-bit inputs; they cannot eliminate loads/branches or fuse three-operand operations like accumulate without a third input.

proposal.title: Requantize int32 to int8 with scale/clamp
proposal.rationale: Replaces ~10 instructions (mul, shift, compares, branches) in requant hotspot (2.75% of dynamic instructions). One custom instruction (5-7 cycles) vs ~30 cycles baseline. Saves ~1.4% total cycles.

proposal.title: Multiply-accumulate two int8 pairs
proposal.rationale: Enables 2-element tail-loop unrolling with accumulate (rs1=acc, rs2=packed pairs). Tail loop currently dead (size%8==0) but would save ~5 cycles/2 elements if activated. Uses two 8x8 multipliers + adder.

proposal.title: Saturated vector add of 4 int8 pairs
proposal.rationale: General-purpose saturated add for activation functions (ReLU, etc.) in other layers. Not used in current FC workload but common in TinyMaix. Four 8-bit adders + saturators, no multipliers.

proposal.title: 4-element int16 dot product
proposal.rationale: Supports int16 layers (e.g., quantized weights). Two 16x16 multipliers (map to 2 DSP blocks) + adder. Distinct from int8 dot4; enables mixed-precision without software emulation.

proposal.title: 4-element int8 dot product with 32-bit reduction
proposal.rationale: Replaces 2x ss_dot2_lo + 2x srli + 3x add per 32-bit word pair (approx 30 cycles) with one 6-cycle instruction. Two calls per 8-element iteration save ~60 cycles/iter (4096 iters = 245k cycles, 1.6x overall speedup). Uses 4 DSP blocks (4x 8x8 multipliers + adder tree) and minimal LUTs.

proposal.title: 2-element int8 dot product on high 16-bit halves
proposal.rationale: Eliminates two srli (3 cycles each) per high-half dot product. Two high-half pairs per 8-element iteration save 12 cycles/iter (49k total, 1.14x speedup) at half the DSP cost of dot4_sum. Composable with existing dot2_lo for a 2-instruction 4-element reduction without shifts.

proposal.title: 32x16 signed multiply returning high 32 bits
proposal.rationale: Fuses the 32x16 multiply (5-6 cycles) and 16-bit arithmetic right-shift (3 cycles) in requant into one 6-cycle instruction. Saves ~3 cycles per requant call. Though requant is only 1.7% of cycles, this instruction costs only 2 DSP blocks (two 8x8 partial products for 32x16 high half) and benefits any fixed-point scaling.

proposal.title: Horizontal add of two 16-bit halves
proposal.rationale: Pure ALU instruction (0 DSP, ~10 LUTs) reducing two 16-bit values in one register to 32-bit sum in 3 cycles vs srli+add (6 cycles). Generic building block for any pairwise reduction (e.g., manual dot2x2 emulation, vector reductions). Negligible area cost.
